messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan (2.8.1) expose_stan_functions compiles code on linux but not on windows
parts:
To get print to work, you need to pass in a stream with the
right name. There are no functions in Stan that print on their
own --- it's only the print statements.

Should I start generating a second Stan file that contains
pure double instantiations of all the template types that aren't
int? It wouldn't be hard to code generate. I'm reluctant to
put it at the top-level of the main Stan program output because
that's very poor programming practice. But I'd be OK generating
a second header file that calls the first that you could use.

I created an issue here:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1703

Should those functions catch all exceptions while they're at it?

I'd rather not have them swallow their print streams.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan (2.8.1) expose_stan_functions compiles code on linux but not on windows
parts:
On Monday, November 23, 2015 at 2:36:31 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Should those functions catch all exceptions while they're at it?
I would say no. If there is an exception, R will throw an error.
I'd rather not have them swallow their print streams.

The print statements used to work, but I apparently broke them when fixing user-defined functions that do ODEs. It should be easy to fix in rstan.

Ben
